To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degeneration pattern of organ of Corti hair cells is closely correlated with CAP N1 thresholds and that the sequence of degeneration is as follows: (1) IHC, (2) afferent nerve fibres, (3) pillar cells, (4) OHC and (5) efferent nerve fibrs.

the degenerative changes in IHCs, OHCs and supporting cells after acoustic overstimulations follow a time sequence and that these changes are closely associated with the time sequence of changes in the afferents.

acoustic trauma results in a progressive degeneration of the organ of the Corti, which starts in the area of the organ corresponding to the exposure level, and that this degeneration is associated with a progressive loss of CAP N1 response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the degeneration of the organ of corti and the development of a new hearing aid for the treatment of tinnitus.
the development of a model for acoustic trauma in the guinea-pig organ of Corti which is suitable for studying the sequence of events following acoustic trauma.
a study of the time sequence of events leading up to degeneration of the organ of corti after acoustic over-stimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the degenerative changes after acoustic overstimulations are not completed after 4-5 weeks.
the degenerative process is a complex one, involving many different types of cells and that the reparative process is a very slow one.
the sequence of degenerative changes in hair cells and their supporting structures after acute acoustic trauma can be divided into two main phases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sequence of degenerative events in the organ of corti after exposure to intense sound is: 1) damage of the stereocilia and hair cell body, 2) degeneration of the afferent dendritic endings and nerve fibres and 3) degeneration of pillar cells and supporting cells, followed by a reparative process.
the sequence of events in the organ of corti following acoustic overstimulation is a progressive degeneration of hair cells and nerve endings followed by reparative processes.
a 3.8 kHz exposure for 22. 5 min to an intensity of 120 dB SPL causes a maximum damage in the organ of corti in a region corresponding to 3.5 kHz.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a clear correlation between hair cell loss and CAP thresholds.
there are many different ways to induce cochlear damage, and the resulting damage patterns are very different.

the degenerative process in the organ after exposure is still ongoing after 4 weeks, and that the development of holes in reticular lamina seems to result in a spread of degeneration to the cells bilateral to the maximum damage.
